key_insight: Chemical gradients in porous and crowded media can actively transport colloids and droplets via diffusiophoresis and diffusioosmosis, sometimes dominating classical hydrodynamic transport mechanisms.
engineering_relevance: These effects matter for predicting and controlling filtration, clogging, contaminant removal, delivery in tissues and gels, and breakthrough/dispersion in porous devices and soils.
method: Reviews the minimal physicochemical model for diffusiophoresis and diffusioosmosis.
Connects gradient generation, stretching, and mixing in porous media to particle transport.
Synthesizes experiments in dead-end pores, flowing pathways, and micromodels.
evidence_signal: The abstract highlights recent experimental results showing orders-of-magnitude changes in breakthrough and dispersion, and enhanced removal from dead-end pores due to prolonged diffuse solute forcing.
watch_item: Model predictions may be sensitive to geometry, solute chemistry, and the transition from 2D algebraic mixing to 3D chaotic mixing in real porous media.
paper_title: Diffusiophoretic transport of colloids and emulsions in complex environments
